Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_with_TemporalField.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestInternationalFixedChronology/TestInternationalFixedChronology_test_with_TemporalField.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

I'll read the original test file and the CUT source to understand the code before improving it.Now I have a full picture. The main understandability issues are:
1. Many unused data-provider methods (dead code in this single-test-method file)
2. Many unused imports
3. The `data_with()` array is a wall of text — all entries on one line
4. No logical grouping/comments in the data

I'll rewrite the file with unused code removed, proper line-per-entry formatting, and logical grouping.The improved test compiled successfully. The refactored file removes all unused data-provider methods and imports, formats each row of `data_with()` on its own line with aligned columns, and adds concise section comments that group entries by scenario (standard date, Year Day, Leap Day, and boundary cases), making the test's intent immediately clear to a reader.
